192825.overview: This road racing game features five stages, taking in day and night driving. Each stage has a variety of twists and turns, blind bends, hills and opponents to avoid. Player controls car with steering, accelerate/brake and can shift between two gears, low and high. The player must reach the stage markers within a time limit to continue. Time bonuses are awarded based on how well the player did.

192826.overview: Tyrann. - Here is a role-playing adventure game that takes you to the medieval village of Golanur. Six characters, created at the start of the game, will act under your orders. Your team formed, it must be armed and protected. Send your characters one by one to the stall. Their fortune varies according to their caste: it is sometimes necessary to combine the money of two of them to arm a third. As for the adventure, two levels of play are available: on side A of the tape, a nine-level maze will allow you to train and meet monsters, each one more deadly than the other. When the team has reached, on average, the eleventh level of experience, the B-side will plunge them into the secret of Tyrann, the real goal of the game.In a labyrinth much larger than the previous one, you will then discover new spells whose meaning will have to be penetrated. Don't let your hit points decrease too much. The great alchemist can easily get you back on your feet but his prices are up to the service he provides you. A captivating game.

203132.overview: This game is a version of the Sega classic Columns with a distinctly Egyptian theme. Columns of three blocks, each engraved with a symbol, fall from the top of the screen, and you must create horizontal, vertical or diagonal lines of three or more matching symbols. It’s a simple concept which is quite similar to Tetris. The graphics are beautifully drawn using the CPC’s four-colour mode, and several playing modes are included – classical, stage mode (achieve a score within a set time limit), time attack (score as many points as possible within three minutes), and a two-player ‘versus’ mode.

203133.overview: A homebrew version of one of the most popular puzzle games of all time for the Amstrad CPC. This version was developed by Epsilon and published by Power System in 1995.

203184.overview: Teodoro No Sabe Volar is a great arcade adventure game that features great graphics, fast-paced gameplay and strong grab factor. The graphics are really cool; something between "Rick Dangerous II" and "Phantomas Saga: Infinity", they have great colours, smooth animation and great sprite design. The scenery is also very detailed. A minus here is the small playing screen. The sound is not the strong point of this game but it is adequate and fairly supports the game. The gameplay is excellent; assisted by the graphics and the good collision detection, the scenery keeps evolving and changing until the game is completed. This is a magnificent, albeit short, gem.

204916.overview:
A space simulation with elements from a number of other genres mixed in. Your mission is to destroy a robot army that has taken over a planet. Gameplay includes arcade sequences, where you fly your ship around and shoot the enemy robots; strategy elements, as you attempt to navigate and locate parts to repair the defense system; and even text-adventure elements, in the form of giving commands to your ship's computer.

There's no real change to the gameplay of the Special Edition but the presentation and detail within the game has been considerably extended.

207155.overview: Trivia UK is a computer quiz game based on the board game Trivial Pursuit where you have to move around a board from two to four players answering questions on six subjects on various small squares. The categories are Entertainment, History, Sport & Leisure, Geography, Arts & Literature and Science & Nature and each subject is coloured coded. The aim is to collect six pieces before your opponents, one from each subject by answering a question correctly on a large square for each category. The squares go round the edge of the board and you can move either left or right. A dice is thrown to see how many squares you can move and if you answer correctly then you move again, the next player moves if you answer incorrectly. You have to say the answer out loud and tell the computer if the answer was right or wrong.

211172.overview: The game was written using GAC and is a reasonably large text adventure with 60 locations with accompanying graphics. Originally released by the author, before being made available through WoW Software. Many of the puzzles don't give quite enough information for the user to determine what needs to be done without a high level of patience and trial and error.

211192.overview:
This adventure software is particularly easy to use. Inspired by interactive role-playing games, Ténèbres does not rely on any graphics, apart from a few rare presentation tables. Without implementing any game logic, Ténèbres relies more on luck than on reflection. Your quest actually consists of a series of questions concerning the direction to take, the objects to find, etc.

 

So it's a matter of selecting your answer to cross the frog pond and reach, for example, the cursed cliff. If it is very easy to perish (one wrong move is enough), it will be wise to save the adventure as often as possible. For a classic scenario, the quest unfortunately relies too much on luck and chance. Logic will never make you guess the intentions of your future encounters and only the experience of a few sudden deaths will allow you to complete the three hours of play announced by the instructions. History suffers somewhat from this eternal uncertainty. We also regret that there is never any question of life points or experience points. Only the simplicity of the game and its handling explains its publication. An excellent way, undoubtedly, to launch the youngest on the road to adventure.

215249.overview:
In a similar manner to Jewels of Darkness and Silicon Dreams, this collection brings together three interlinked Level 9 adventures:

    Lords of Time
    Red Moon
    The Price of Magik

and attempts to turn them into a single experience.  The games have all been updated into the company's later adventure system, and have longer textual descriptions and some slight puzzle tweaks

215401.overview:
Compete as either England or a World XI in a test match environment featuring the full rules of cricket and giving you the opportunity to bat, bowl and field.

Later re-released by Alternative Software as Cricket International.

215550.overview:
You Top Secret mission is to penetrate a nuclear installation in order to stop the launch of a deadly missile strike.  

Written with the Graphic Adventure Creator and released as part of a double pack with Mountains of Ket, this is a fairly basic GAC adventure with short location descriptions and some frustrating instant death screens.

215675.overview:
Grrr is the rather oddly named compilation of two arcade game clones previously published for the BBC Micro and converted to the CPC.

Killer Gorilla is a clone of Donkey Kong while Gauntlet is a replica of Defender (somewhat confusingly).

Neither game was published on its own for the CPC but only released first as part of this double pack and then latterly as makeweights in the first pair of '10 Computer Hits' (and 6 Computer Hits) compilations from Beau Jolly.

216627.overview: Toki is an awesome arcade shooter platformer that was released way back in 1989 by a designer by the name of Akira Sakuma for many different retro systems. In it you played as an enhanced Ape transformed from a Human that could shoot energy balls from his mouth defeating strange creatures and finally an evil Wizard.

218142.overview: Total Eclipse II: The Sphinx Jinx a reworking of Total Eclipse sharing many of the same locations, using the Freescape system and vector graphics. To eliminate an ancient curse the player must find 12 pieces of the sphinx within two hours, hidden in the underground passages beneath the pyramid. Except of numerous puzzles the player will face mummies, poisoned darts or heat exhaustion caused by limited access to the water supply. No objects may be collected, although encountered gold bars can significantly enlarge the assets

218283.overview: Helicopters show up in front of the base you are defending, and paratroopers begin to jump. Your mission is to take down, as much as possible of them, before they invade you.

219334.overview:
The first compilation of what would become the 'They Sold a Million' series. The included games are: 

* Daley Thompson's Decathlon (Ocean) 
* Beach-Head (U.S. Gold) [EXC. GERMAN VERSION]
* Jet Set Willy (Software Projects)
* Sabre Wulf (Ultimate Play The Game)
* Rocco (Gremlin) [GERMAN VERSION ONLY]

For the Amstrad CPC version, both Daley Thompson & Beach-Head were relatively new releases (within six months) when this compilation was released.  Meanwhile Sabre Wulf was published in tandem with this release meaning players could buy it on its own or as part of the compilation.  Also of note, the version of Jet Set Willy on this release was different from the initial CPC release - dubbed 'The Final Frontier' on other machines and sold as Jet Set Willy II, the expanded JSW was actually the initial CPC release - the version on this compilation is the 'original' cut down game that had first appeared on the Spectrum.

Finally, owing to German sensitivities of games that featured war like settings and dictatorships at the time, Beach-Head was replaced by Rocco for the German release - the boxing game was also a brand new release on the CPC at the time.

219524.overview:
The second in the 'They Sold a Million' series sees a similar approach to the first selection of games with a mix of game types from different publishers.

Included games are:

* Bruce Lee (U.S. Gold)
* Match Day (Ocean)
* Knight Lore (Ultimate)
* Match Point (Psion)

219540.overview:
Coded by Anthony Collins, Theseus is one of the first independent releases made using the Graphic Adventure Creator (GAC).  

Based on the Greek myth of Theseus and the Minotaur, the game sees you take the titular role as you begin your hero's journey of freeing the isle of Crete by destroying the beast.

A two part adventure divided by a password.

219917.overview:
Released exclusively as part of the Cascade 50 games collections (Cassette 50 and Disc 50).  Not to be confused with the Black Knight Software 'Checkman' clone released around the same time.

Time-Bomb asks a series of mathematical questions with a strict limit.  To win the game you need to avoid making mistakes and keep answering quickly.

219933.overview:
Released exclusively as part of the Cascade 50 games collections (Cassette 50 and Disc 50).

Trucking is a trading and company management simulation where you look to build your fortune by buying and selling the right goods at the right time.

219951.overview:
Released exclusively as part of the Cascade 50 games collections (Cassette 50 and Disc 50).

Three Card Brag sees both players each dealt three cards face down. There is a single round of betting, with each player having the option of betting or folding. If there was a previous bet, the player must contribute at least that much more to the pot.  The player may the double the previous bet to see the dealer's hand. At this point, the two hands are revealed, and the player with the better hand takes the entire pot. If there is a tie, the player who is seeing loses.

219990.overview:
A collection of three educational mini-games from Macmillan aimed at pre-school kids.

Sam Goes Shopping tasks the player with finding the right shop that sells a particular item and the department within it.

Computer Snap is a colourful card matching game where youngsters have to match two pictures before the computer or their opponent.

Tables Test is an opportunity for kids to test themselves on their knowledge of the times tables.

220017.overview:
Compilation of three games that were previously released as full price games

Games included were:

* Airwolf II
* Great Gurianos
* 3DC

220056.overview:
Ten Great Games is the first in a series of three compilation packs from Gremlin for the Amstrad CPC.

Games included were:

* Avenger
* Future Knight
* Krakout
* Bounder
* Footballer of the Year
* Trailblazer
* Highway Encounter
* Monty on the Run
* West Bank
* Jack the Nipper

271888.overview:
A compilation of eight titles, all licenced from Taito arcade cabs.  All were originally published by Ocean under their Imagine label except for Flying Shark and Bubble Bobble which had both been put out by Firebird.

Games included were:

* Slap Fight
* Rastan
* Legend of Kage

* Bubble Bobble
* Arkanoid
* Arkanoid: Revenge of Doh
* Rastan

308389.overview:
A compilation of the three J.R.R. Tolkien inspired text adventures available on the Amstrad CPC, covering the first two volumes of The Lord of the Rings novels and their prequel.  All three were originally published by the, by now, defunct Melbourne House.

* The Hobbit
* The Lord of the Rings: Game One
* The Shadows of Mordor: Game Two of Lord of the Rings

312594.overview:
A compilation of ten titles, from Elite Systems primarily published by themselves in the first instance but with a few others that they picked up for their Encore, re-release label.  Notably, the entire contents of their earlier 'The Story So Far Vol 2' compilation was also featured on this collection.

Games included were:

* Space Harrier
* Overlander
* Live and Let Die
* Beyond the Ice Palace
* Hopping Mad
* Thundercats
* Buggy Boy
* Dragon's Lair
* Great Gurianos
* Ikari Warriors

353854.overview:
The Test is a text only adventure written by Ken Bond with the Professional Adventure Writer programme.

As a prospective member of the EFF (Elite Fighting Force) you are parachuted into a testing area where you must use your wits to survive the various traps that have been set for you and solve the mystery within.

396031.overview:
Compilation of five 'explosive hits' from Domark - all arcade conversions published originally under the Tengen label.

Games included are:

* Toobin'
* Dragon Spirit
* APB
* Hard Drivin'
* Xybots

417577.overview:
You are Tizpan, a regular hero type who just happens to live in a bamboo hut in the jungle in deepest darkest South America.  Untouched by outside contact, you survive in domestic bliss with the lovely Jayne, a lady savage.  Waking one morning to find that she is gone, and given the signs of struggle it doesn't seem as if it's her choice, you set out to find her and bring her home safely to your hut.

A text only adventure written using The Quill utility.

417685.overview:
Robert Louis Stevenson's seminal adventure novel of life on the high seas, buccaneers and buried gold was ripe for a computerised retelling.  With characters and plot points that have transcended into popular culture (such as Long John Silver, The Black Spot and Ben Gunn) and is arguably responsible for what everyone automatically thinks of when they think of pirates.

This text only adventure looks to recapture the atmosphere of Stevenson's novel (which by this point had entered the public domain).

448429.overview: Torreoscura is an original conversational adventure by Bieno Marti made with The Quill (Gilsoft) in its versions for Commodore 64, Amstrad CPC and ORIC and with DAAD (Adventures AD) in its ports for ZX Spectrum, MSX, Amstrad PCW and PC MS- TWO CGA.

462746.overview:
Target Ball is an arcade-style maze game  in which up to three players race to complete nine clockwise laps around each of six stages. The goal is simple—circle the arena faster than your opponents—but frequent obstacles and the game’s unpredictable rebound physics make each run difficult to control.

The game takes place on single-screen arenas viewed from above. Players guide small balls through narrow corridors that loop around the screen, with motion governed by inertia and wall collisions. Hazards modify control and movement: bombs freeze the player briefly, puddles cause uncontrolled sliding, teleporters move the ball elsewhere, and “joystick” icons reverse directional input. Completing nine full laps clears the stage. The game’s challenge lies in maintaining control as speed increases and rebounds multiply.
